title: Alternating Cech total complex of a quasi-coherent complex computes derived sections
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] with a finite open covering $X=\bigcup_{i=1}^r U_i$, allowing $r=0$, such that every intersection $U_{i_0}\cap\cdots\cap U_{i_p}$ indexed by a nonempty tuple (including repetitions and empty opens) is affine. Let $F^\bullet$ be an unbounded cochain complex of quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-modules [pqf-def-coherent] viewed by localization in $D(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-pc-derived-category]. Let $T_{\mathcal U}(F^\bullet)$ and $\alpha$ be the alternating Cech total functor and its global-section augmentation of [def-sc-alternating-cech-total-complex], with Cech degree first and total differential $d_1+(-1)^p d_2$. Write $R\Gamma$ for the unbounded right derived functor of the module-valued global sections functor [def-sc-ringed-space-module-cohomology]. Then (i) there exists a map $\beta_F:QT_{\mathcal U}(F^\bullet)\to R\Gamma(QF^\bullet)$ satisfying $\operatorname{IsAlternatingCechDerivedComparison}(\mathcal U,F^\bullet,\beta_F)$, the canonical-map equation through every K-injective resolution; (ii) every map satisfying that equation is an isomorphism in $D(\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X))$; and (iii) for every morphism $g:F^\bullet\to G^\bullet$ of complexes of quasi-coherent modules and comparisons $\beta_F,\beta_G$, one has $\beta_G\circ Q(T_{\mathcal U}(g))=R\Gamma(Qg)\circ\beta_F$. Thus the canonical map of Stacks lemma-alternating-cech-complex-complex is an isomorphism, functorial in $F^\bullet$, without boundedness assumptions.

proof.text: Use the existing functorial K-injective resolution I and its natural quasi-isomorphism eta. Write A=Q Gamma, B=Q T_U, and D=R Gamma Q as functors on complexes. Let a:A to B be the localized augmentation and b:A to D the derived-functor unit transported through quotientCompQhIso. On every K-injective J, b_J is exactly the inverse of rightDerivedFunctorObjQIso(J). The augmentation lemma makes I(a) invertible, and D(eta) is invertible because eta is a quasi-isomorphism. Define the natural transformation beta=B(eta), followed by inverse I(a), followed by I(b), followed by inverse D(eta). All inverses are of explicit natural transformations, and no arbitrary existence witness is chosen.

Prove a_K followed by beta_K equals b_K, for every complex K: compose with the invertible D(eta_K), use naturality of a at eta_K to cancel a_IK, and use naturality of b at eta_K. For K-injective J, cancellation by the invertible a_J and b_J equals epsilon_J inverse gives beta_J followed by epsilon_J followed by a_J equals identity. Naturality of beta at any K-injective resolution i:K to J now proves the defining comparison equation. Hence beta_F exists and satisfies IsAlternatingCechDerivedComparison through every resolution.

For quasi-coherent F, the affine-cover resolution lemma makes B(eta_F) invertible. The remaining three factors in beta_F are invertible: I(a) by augmentation, I(b) by the unit computation on the K-injective resolution, and D(eta) by localization. Thus beta_F is invertible.

Every other comparison gamma on a complex K equals beta_K. Apply their defining equations to eta_K:K to I(K), then cancel D(eta_K), epsilon_IK and a_IK, each invertible. Consequently every comparison on F is invertible. For any g:F to G and supplied comparisons, replace them by beta_F and beta_G using uniqueness, and apply naturality of the constructed natural transformation beta. No homotopy choice or additional naturality lemma is needed for this categorical glue.

statement_change.old_statement: Let $U$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] with a finite open covering $\mathcal U:U=\bigcup_{i=1}^rU_i$ such that $U_{i_0\ldots i_p}=U_{i_0}\cap\cdots\cap U_{i_p}$ is affine for all $p\ge0$ and all $i_0,\ldots,i_p$. Let $\mathcal F^\bullet$ be a cochain complex of quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_U$-modules [pqf-def-coherent], not assumed bounded in either direction. Let $\operatorname{Tot}(\check{\mathcal C}^\bullet_{\mathrm{alt}}(\mathcal U,\mathcal F^\bullet))$ be the total complex of the double complex with terms $\check{\mathcal C}^p_{\mathrm{alt}}(\mathcal U,\mathcal F^q)=\prod_{i_0<\cdots<i_p}\mathcal F^q(U_{i_0\ldots i_p})$, the alternating Cech differential $d_1$ [def-weil-pbc-site-cech-complex] in the $p$-direction, the differential $d_2$ induced by $\mathcal F^\bullet$ in the $q$-direction, and total differential $d_1+(-1)^pd_2$ on the $(p,q)$ term. Then there is a canonical isomorphism $\operatorname{Tot}(\check{\mathcal C}^\bullet_{\mathrm{alt}}(\mathcal U,\mathcal F^\bullet))\to R\Gamma(U,\mathcal F^\bullet)$ in $D(\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U))$ [def-pc-derived-category] [def-pc-derived-direct-image], functorial in $\mathcal F^\bullet$.
statement_change.what: The old statement described the total complex and canonical map informally, but no recorded dependency defined the alternating total functor for a general scheme or its canonical comparison. The full-site Cech complex is indexed by all tuples, and the principal-open construction is only a Spec A specialization. Quantifying over an arbitrary Tot unrelated to this construction would not express the source. The correction supplies an explicit construction and the equation through every K-injective resolution, then spells out existence, invertibility of every comparison, and functoriality; the mathematical hypotheses and result are unchanged.
